_comment: WO-4 paired device pilot, mps half, approved explicitly by the owner (2026-10-05): cell 0b
exactly as wo4-cell0b-pilot-6pct.json, seed 42, trained on the Mac's GPU (mps). Its CPU
counterpart is wo4-cell0b-pair-cpu-6pct.json, run on the same code version (main at c07b4e0
plus WO-4, after WO-2's training-parity fix), one after the other and never together.
NOT A RESULT OF RECORD; MEASURED TO PROPOSE THE D6 TOLERANCE. ADR 0020's 2026-10-05
amendment requires the accepted CPU-vs-GPU difference in warm recall@500 to be stated
before any non-CPU run counts; no tolerance is stated yet, so this run is the measurement
that proposes one. Its recall is cited nowhere but its run record.
Training runs on mps; the trained weights are moved to the CPU before anything is scored,
so the probe, the per-pass holdout diagnostic and the final evaluation are all computed on
the CPU. Same seed: the negatives come from the same NumPy stream, but dropout draws from
the mps generator, while on the CPU run it shares the CPU generator with the shuffle. From
pass 2 the two runs therefore see examples in different orders. Recorded: the speed-up per
pass (CPU epoch_train_seconds over mps) and over the whole fit, and the difference in warm
recall@500 against the pair's CPU run. Predeclared checks as for the CPU runs: protocol hash,
exact cold recall, probe below the cutoff.
result_status: not a result of record; measured to propose the D6 tolerance

projection.measured: 2026-10-05, 60 optimizer steps of this cell on the O-25 6% partition, steady-state steps 11-60, one thread, load average about 3.9 with two other 6% pilots running
projection.basis: 3 to 5 passes at the measured step time, plus data load and per-pass probe and holdout scoring
